papers.title: Center anomalies without twists: torsion, exact degeneracies, and condensates
papers.abstract: Mixed center anomalies are usually exposed by 't Hooft's twisted boundary conditions in a Hamiltonian formalism. On $\mathbb {RP}^3$, torsion makes the twist unnecessary: a center operator on the untwisted $SU(2)$ Hilbert space anticommutes with time reversal in Yang-Mills theory at $\theta=\pi$ and with the chiral symmetry of super Yang-Mills theory, so every level is at least doubly degenerate. The relevant semiclassical object is the BPST instanton, which descends to a charge-$\tfrac12$ saddle on the orbifold $\mathbb R^4/\mathbb Z_2$. We complete it in two ways: applying a conformal transformation maps the orbifold to $\mathbb R\times\mathbb {RP}^3$, with the saddle describing the tunneling event between the two center sectors; by resolving the orbifold singularity, we obtain the Eguchi-Hanson space, which gives the gaugino condensate at its weak-coupling value.

papers.title: Anomaly inflow for simplicial K\"{a}hler fermions
papers.abstract: We study massive K\"{a}hler Dirac fermions propagating on finite triangulations of various three dimensional manifolds with one or more boundaries. To probe the anomaly structure of these models we decompose the K\"{a}hler field into two reduced K\"{a}hler fields and choose boundary conditions that ensure that any edge modes are necessarily massless. We then show how to factorize the Pfaffian of this system into a product of bulk and boundary sectors each of which can separately pick up a phase under a global $Z_4$ transformation of the fermions that simultaneously changes the sign of the mass. These phases are topological, depending only on the index of the lattice K\"{a}hler operator in that sector. For the boundary sector a non-trivial phase signals the presence of a 't Hooft anomaly. We study cases where the boundary is anomalous but an inflow from the bulk cancels its phase. Canceling this anomaly for a non-orientable boundary in the absence of the bulk recovers the known classification of topological superconductors. We also give a continuum interpretation of these results in terms of inflow from a gravitational Chern Simons theory which is induced by integrating out massive bulk K\"{a}hler Dirac fermions. In the presence of a boundary the latter gives rise to Wen-Zee terms that mediate the anomaly inflow mechanism.

papers.title: Quantum phase transition and superselection sectors in two-color one-flavor matrix QCD at weak coupling
papers.abstract: We numerically investigate the weak-coupling (small $g$) regime of the matrix model of $SU(2)$ gauge theory coupled to one flavor of massless fundamental quarks. The theory possesses a global Pauli-G\"ursey $SU(2)_B$ symmetry, which organizes physical states of spin $J$ into sectors labelled by its representation $B$. We find localization-delocalization quantum phase transitions (QPTs) in multiple $(B,J)$ sectors at sector-dependent critical couplings $g_\ast^{BJ}$. Direct evaluation of the localization probability reveals that the ground states are predominantly localized near $A_i=0$ for $g<g_\ast^{BJ}$, but become almost entirely expelled from this region for $g>g_*^{BJ}$. The QPTs in different sectors exhibit distinct features, and we establish that quark-glue interactions are essential for these transitions. The transitions are singular: the ground state expectation value of $\text{Tr}(A_iA_i)$ remains finite for $g< g_\ast^{BJ}$, whereas it diverges as $g$ approaches $g_\ast^{BJ}$ from above. We show that the two limiting ground states on either side of $g_\ast^{BJ}$ belong to distinct superselection sectors. Furthermore, as $g$ approaches $g_\ast^{BJ}$ from above, the ground state localizes on a submanifold (of codimension 2) of the gauge configuration space, with the spin and color of its glue components becoming locked.

papers.title: Quantum vacuum inversion and multi-kink unbinding in the non-degenerate double sine-Gordon model
papers.abstract: Quantum fluctuations can unbind a composite soliton while the correction to its mass stays small. We show this beyond perturbation theory for the multi-kinks of the non-degenerate double sine-Gordon model. At one loop the vacuum at the centre of the multi-kink becomes the true vacuum at a coupling of order the classical lifting of the vacua. Tensor-network calculations of the lattice theory show that this inversion survives beyond one loop and has a continuum limit, and that the Gaussian effective potential captures it. On finite chains the multi-kink unbinds when the tension of the string of central vacuum between its two halves falls through zero

papers.title: Vacuum correlations of the stress-energy-momentum tensor with constituent quarks
papers.abstract: The two point correlation function of the stress-energy-momentum tensor describes the propagation of a space-time ``micro-earthquake'' in the vacuum. In the framework of the path integral formulation of field theory in curved space-time, we discuss the Ward-Takashi identity for two-point Green's function of the stress-energy-momentum tensor for a general case of a non-conformal theory. The identity constrains the longitudinal part of the correlator, with the vacuum expectation value of the stress-energy-momentum, non-zero in a non-conformal theory. The obtained formula is demonstrated on the free massive Dirac fermion theory, treated at the one-loop level. This example befits a class of phenomenological chiral quarks models which have been used successfully in numerous applications in the soft non-perturbative regime of strong interactions. We stress the role of the constraints following from the Ward-Takahashi identity for the correlation functions in these models and point out the differences with the low-energy theorems (sum rules), not complying to the symmetry requirements. We also show the temporal representation of the two-point correlators, which is an object amenable to lattice QCD simulations.

papers.title: Particle seismology: mechanical and gravitational properties from parton-hadron duality
papers.abstract: The internal structure of hadrons is characterized by form factors which correspond to matrix elements of currents. Among those, the stress-energy-momentum tensor is a universally conserved quantity providing the gravitational form factors, from which mechanical properties may be derived via the response to the space-time fluctuations. They have received much attention because of their role as moments of the Generalized Parton Distributions, where the stress-energy-momentum tensor couples to two photons, and more recently, due to the explicit lattice QCD determination for the pion and nucleon. In these lectures we attempt a pedagogical review of the topic from a purely hadronic point of view, based on the notion of dispersion relations, meson dominance, and parton-hadron duality. We show that despite the overwhelming simplicity of the approach, a rather successful description of the lattice QCD data is achieved.

papers.title: Dispersive analysis of the $\boldsymbol{J/\psi \to \gamma \pi^0 \pi^0}$ process
papers.abstract: We present a dispersive amplitude analysis of the low-energy $\pi^0\pi^0$ system in the radiative decay $J/\psi\to\gamma\pi^0\pi^0$, using the mass-independent BESIII $0^{++}$ and $2^{++}$ intensities, the total spectrum, and the measured $0^{++}-2^{++}$ $E1$ phase difference. The isoscalar $S$-wave is described by a coupled-channel $\pi\pi/K\bar K$ Muskhelishvili-Omn\`es representation, which implements the strong final-state interactions associated with the $f_0(500)$ and $f_0(980)$. The $D$-wave is treated with a single-channel $\pi\pi$ Muskhelishvili-Omn\`es representation, where we identify all kinematic constraints of helicity amplitudes before transforming them to the experimental $E1$, $M2$, and $E3$ multipoles. Smooth short-distance production of a pseudoscalar-meson pair is encoded in subtraction polynomials, while left-hand-cut effects are estimated and found to be numerically subleading. We identify the negative solution of the BESIII $0^{++}-2^{++}$ $E1$ phase ambiguity, after using the modulo-$\pi$ freedom of production amplitudes, as the phase solution compatible with unitarity constraints, showing that the measured phase information can be accommodated with the Omn\`es phase motion without requiring large additional phases. By normalizing the BESIII intensities with the extracted branching fraction, we fix the absolute scale of the fitted amplitudes, making them suitable as input for future dispersive studies of two-pion contributions to gravitational form factors.

papers.title: Amplified Isospin Breaking from Coupled-Channel Dynamics Near Threshold
papers.abstract: We identify the dynamical origin of amplified isospin breaking in near-threshold states. Using a pole-residue-based measure defined directly from the pole couplings, rather than from decay observables that are also affected by different final-state kinematics, we show that threshold proximity of the pole alone is insufficient: large isospin breaking requires a sizable interaction in the companion isospin channel. In particular, the isospin-violating pole-coupling ratio vanishes when the companion-channel interaction is switched off, even at finite threshold splitting. Applied to the $X(3872)$, the observed large isospin breaking points to a nearby partner pole, $W_{c1}$, as predicted in previous studies. As a concrete realization of the previously discussed leading/shadow-pole interchange, we find that the $W_{c1}$ pole, which predominantly affects the line shapes near the charged threshold in the physical case, does not evolve into the pure $I=1$ eigenstate in the isospin limit; instead, that eigenstate is continuously connected to a more distant shadow pole.

papers.title: Reassessing the $X(2370)$ in $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$ beyond the one-dimensional mass projections
papers.abstract: The BESIII Collaboration recently extracted the properties of the $X(2370)$ from a fit to the one-dimensional $K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$ invariant-mass spectrum in $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$. The intermediate two-body structures visible in the mass correlations, including the $K_0^*(1430)$ bands, require a coherent treatment of cross-channel interference when interpreting the enhancement near 2.3 GeV. We reassess the need for an additional $X(2370)$ contribution by fitting the published data using an effective coupled-channel framework with an approximate detection efficiency depending on the three-body invariant mass. The three-body parent amplitude is parameterized using a $K$-matrix that describes scattering among several quasi-two-body channels. The seven- and eight-bare-state models give similar mass distributions. Adding the eighth bare state lowers the Poisson deviance by 1.22% and produces an additional pole at $E=(2419-i152)$ MeV, substantially broader than the $X(2370)$ mass-width reference. This pole is model-dependent, and its identification with the $X(2370)$ is not clear. The present analysis does not establish the need for an additional $X(2370)$ contribution in $J/\psi\to\gamma K_S^0K_S^0\pi^0$, thereby weakening the flavor-singlet argument based on the suppression of $K^*\bar K$ relative to the total $K\bar K\pi$ contribution. A more comprehensive experimental amplitude analysis, incorporating coherent interference, mass and angular correlations, and detector effects across related decay channels, is needed to establish the role and decay properties of the $X(2370)$.

papers.title: Proton generalized parton distributions from electromagnetic form factors: A theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction
papers.abstract: We present a theoretically constrained phenomenological reconstruction of the unpolarized, chiral-even, leading-twist proton generalized parton distributions $H^q$ and $E^q$. At zero skewness, valence-quark distributions are combined with flavor-dependent exponential profiles calibrated simultaneously against phenomenological representations of the proton and neutron electromagnetic form factors. The construction imposes exact valence and anomalous-magnetic-moment normalizations, the low-scale condition $B^{u+d}(0)=0$, the required endpoint behavior, and the complete Gaussian impact-parameter positivity bound. The resulting parametrization provides a reasonable description of the electromagnetic form factors and their slopes while revealing the tension between strict GPD consistency and a precision reproduction of all low-$Q^2$ observables within the adopted ansatz. We extend the distributions to nonzero skewness using normalized double distributions and introduce an independent $D$-term to complete the relevant Mellin polynomials. We examine electromagnetic and energy--momentum-tensor form factors, impact-parameter distributions, positivity, polynomiality, and illustrative mechanical properties. The analysis distinguishes information constrained by electromagnetic data from additional assumptions governing skewness and the mechanical sector, thereby providing a transparent elastic baseline for future studies of nucleon-to-resonance transition GPDs.
